description: A body POSTed to /hub/api/read, /hub/api/write or /hub/api/execute ({type, params}, Komodo's API shape, inputs/komodo-template.md), or the hub's answer to one. daemon_body.description: A daemon's JSON answer, passed through unchanged (C-10.17), whole: in result.daemon on success, in error.daemon (with error.daemon_status) on a refusal. Its shape is web-chat's; the route that produced it is named by the request type. When the connector refused (05 C-05.30) it is the connector's body as received: 04's refusal body with authority, or {ok: false, connector: true, reason: 'not-running'} (C-10.17).

cookie.description: A user session (03 C-03.5, C-03.6): the cookie __Host-swc_s on the hub apex, as the shell and the phone send it. With it the request passes the CSRF rule of 04 C-04.23. Exactly one of this or the x-api-key pair is present.

x-api-key.description: An API key's id (03 C-03.7, schemas/03-credential.json api_key): a user's key, or svc_home's key for Home's MCP server (C-03.16). Sent with x-api-secret.

x-api-secret.description: The API key's secret (03 C-03.7): sws_ and 43 base64url characters.

x-swc-api.description: The API major version the client speaks (C-10.29).

x-request-id.description: Optional client id for the request, echoed as request_id; the hub mints one when absent.

idempotency-key.description: On /write and /execute: the same key within 24 hours answers the first result without acting again (C-10.11).

headers.description: Request headers, lowercase as Node reads them. Authentication is one of contract 03's two hub-API credentials (C-03.5 to C-03.7, C-03.16): the user session cookie, or an API key as X-Api-Key plus X-Api-Secret. There is no bearer form; one would be an addition to 03-credential.json first.

type.description: The request type; its group is the path (C-10.12).

params.description: The type's params; {} when it takes none.

type.description: The request's type, echoed when the body named one.

code.description: The error word. Clients treat an unknown word as a generic failure (C-10.29).

hint.description: What to do next, written for the person reading it, as web-chat's refusal hints are.

field.description: bad_request: the first bad field, as a JSON pointer into params.

need.description: forbidden: what the type needs (a level on a chat, a role, or a principal kind).

daemon_status.description: A relayed answer: the HTTP status as the hub received it, the daemon's or the connector's own refusal (05 C-05.30), beside the body in daemon (C-10.17).

error.description: The error shape every type shares. HTTP status per code is in C-10.13. A relayed answer maps by status first (C-10.17): a 2xx with ok:false is refused, 404 not_found, 403 forbidden with need (logged as a second lock), 400 or 415 internal, 503 unavailable, 500 relay_failed; each carries daemon and daemon_status. A relayed answer can be the connector's (05 C-05.30): a 403 whose body carries 04's authority object is forbidden, logged as a connector refusal, never a second lock; a 404 whose body is {ok: false, connector: true, reason: 'not-running'} is the connector's not_found, never the daemon's. A 502 is relay_failed and a 504 relay_timeout. Any other status is relay_failed. daemon_status is the status as the hub received it.
